items.title: "Surprise me" link is shown in the filter panel of the unfiltered catalog
covers: AC1: link "Surprise me" next to the brand and type filters
items.reason: AC1 requires a "Surprise me" link next to the brand and type filters. Its placement only exists in rendered markup of the WebApp, so this is an e2e case; it is separate from the click cases so a missing or misplaced link is reported on its own.

items.title: Without filters, "Surprise me" opens the product page of a catalog product
covers: AC2: no filter, click opens the product page of one of the catalog's products
items.reason: AC2's core outcome is that the click lands on a real product page. The pick and redirect happen server-side, so only an e2e run through the WebApp proves the click reaches `/item/{id}` and renders the product.

items.title: Repeated "Surprise me" clicks open different products
covers: AC2: chosen at random each time
items.reason: AC2 requires a new random pick on each click. A regression that caches the pick, or always picks index 0, would still pass TC-PRB-13-02; this case catches it. It needs real navigation from the catalog page, so e2e.

items.title: With a brand selected, every surprise product belongs to that brand
covers: AC3: brand selected, product opened is one the filter lists
items.reason: AC3 requires the pick to respect the brand filter. A small brand makes the allowed set exact and checkable: brand XE lists 3 products, so any product outside them is a failure. Repeated clicks reduce the chance an unfiltered pick passes by luck (1 in 34 per click).

items.title: With a type selected, every surprise product is one the filtered list shows
covers: AC3: type selected, product opened is one the filter lists
items.reason: AC3 covers a type filter on its own ("brand and/or type"). Type Cycling lists 9 products, which fit exactly on one catalog page, so the test can compare the opened product against the names the page itself lists.

items.title: With brand and type selected that list one product, "Surprise me" always opens that product
covers: AC4 boundary: filters listing exactly one product still show the link
items.reason: AC3 covers brand and type together; a combination listing a single product makes the expected result deterministic. It is also the just-inside boundary of AC4 (one product: the link must still be shown), opposite TC-PRB-13-07.

items.title: Filters that list no product hide the "Surprise me" link
covers: AC4: filters that list no product hide the link
items.reason: AC4 is the only negative outcome the story states: with nothing to pick, the link must not be offered. It is the just-outside boundary (0 products) of TC-PRB-13-06 (1 product); a broken guard would offer a link that leads nowhere.

items.title: The rest of the catalog page is unchanged
covers: AC5: header, filters, product list, paging unchanged
items.reason: AC5 guards against the new slot in the shared `CatalogSearch` component disturbing the rest of the page. It checks each named area (header, filters, product list, paging) against the seeded catalog's known values, on e2e because only the rendered page shows them together.

items.reason: Each per-click demo.highlight(pageHeading, 'Click i: item N', 800) keyframe is a fully blank white page, so the frame contradicts its label. The step-end frames right after show the product page with captions such as 'Click 1: /item/20', and the final highlight shows 'Ids: 20, 27, 45, 91, 82, 38, 71, 86, 3, 29 -> 10 distinct', so the case is proven. Let the product page settle (for example waitForLoadState or the API-name check TC-02 does) before highlighting, so the per-click frames show the product.

The page-2 frames show the current-page indicator and Surprise me link, but none displays the resulting URL. The source calls demo.caption with page.url(), yet that caption is absent from the navigation step, subsequent highlights and final frames. Make the resulting ?page=2 URL readable in recorded evidence, as required by lesson L2.
